text:
elena: Heads up — Solstice Health (prod) reporting intermittent 429s starting ~08:42 UTC. They say it comes in short bursts (~30s) then quiets. They captured a few responses and a replay.

mohit: Can you paste a sample request/response and the raw snippet from the logs?

elena: Paste from their replay: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-ephem-XXXXX\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"model":"opt-1.3b","input":"sample"}'
```
Response they got: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"per_minute_limit exceeded"}
```
Logs show repeated identical requests using the same ephemeral token with ~180 requests in a few seconds window.

ryan-s: Sounds like a fanout lambda or job reusing one token across many concurrent invocations. Do they confirm multiplexing?

elena: Yes — they run a serverless fanout that reuses a single ephemeral key for all child invocations. The token-level RPM/TPM spikes past the per-minute bucket for ~10s bursts and then drops.

lara: Interim advice to customer: enable jittered exponential backoff, avoid simultaneous retries, and if possible rotate to multiple short-lived API keys so concurrency is sharded across keys. Also recommend connection reuse / HTTP keepalive to reduce overhead.

lara: Also sending this to infra: can we pull the token history so we can confirm exact peak numbers? @rate-limit-bot any details?

rate-limit-bot: Token sk-ephem-XXXXX — per_minute_limit=600, current_minute=754 (peak at 08:43:12 UTC), sliding_window shows concentrated burst: 180 calls over 3s, 320 calls over a 15s span during the incident.

mohit: That pattern will trip our per-minute bucket even though average looks okay. For serverless fanout, recommend either: 1) give them multiple API keys and round-robin, 2) switch to a dedicated tenant (Dedicated) for guaranteed throughput, or 3) implement client-side concurrency limits + randomized start delays.

mohit: We can also temporarily raise their token per-minute quota while they roll out fixes.

ryan-s: I applied a +300/min temporary bump to tenant solstice-01 for 2 hours (audit: rw-action-4521). Please verify with the customer. :thumbsup:

elena: Customer just confirmed errors subsided after the bump. They will add jitter/backoff and plan key rotation. I'll send a follow-up email with suggested client patterns and a short playbook for serverless deployments.

mohit: Notes for KB: "Ephemeral token fanout causing per-minute bursts" — key points: do not reuse one ephemeral token across high concurrency, prefer multiple tokens or Dedicated, implement jittered exponential backoff, randomize token selection when rotating keys, and monitor token-level RPM spikes not just averages.

ryan-s: Filing internal follow-up RW-429-ephemeral-token-burst to look at better detection/alerts for concentrated short bursts vs steady load.

elena: Adding reproduction steps and customer-provided request timestamps to the ticket. Closing the immediate triage, will keep an eye for recurrence. :white_check_mark:
